# Retrospective

## Worked

Fresh verified reviewer sessions and neutral equivalent scope preserved independence. Both finals were saved before either was read. Inspecting both modes of a toggle exposed a concrete removal-path regression while acknowledging the intended creation protection. Source-only review was sufficient to establish the finding; synthetic baseline/head evidence corroborated rather than pretending to verify hardware. No desktop resource was needed.

## Friction and deviations

See EVIDENCE-AUDIT.md for full inventory. Partial-clone archive setup failed once, then assignment-private prefetch materialized required objects; failed raw evidence preserved. No fixture executed in failed setup. Fixture guard/producer/redirect retention gaps prohibit a blanket compliance claim. Sol's broad one-line JSON read triggered native automatic output persistence outside assignment, with public tree and local listing metadata; aggregate parallel policy reads exceeded 60 lines. Native history retained. These are process deviations, not grounds to discard independently established source ordering.

## Corrective instructions

Parse one-line JSON into bounded selected fields before printing. Count policy read lines across parallel calls or read serially. Before running, prefetch needed partial-clone objects into the private clone with separate stdout/stderr/exit receipts. Explicitly assert summary/results and each stub/receipt target before writes; gate grep errors and substitution producers separately; retain backend output and caller-side exit even when production redirects. Compare literal target/producer inventory with fixture and output inventory during synthesis. Never describe a successful seal as proof of guard compliance. Do not add substitute experiments once source establishes the useful conclusion.

No confirmed review-tool defect. Partial-clone archive behavior is a documentation opportunity rather than a demonstrated tool bug. No Omadev session or native hardware used. All evidence retained; reviewer panes preserved. Only the outer assistant may publish or select subsequent work.
comment:
The new Surface refusal also prevents removing an existing direct-boot entry.

**Verified:** At `51e06fb`, a `Microsoft Corporation` BIOS vendor is rejected before entry creation, as intended, once the UEFI and `efibootmgr` prerequisites pass.

## Keep removal available for previously created entries

In [`bin/omarchy-setup-direct-boot`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/51e06fbec184897e5c604da3bfa05b697d75f523/bin/omarchy-setup-direct-boot#L16-L41), the new guard exits before the existing-entry lookup. For a matching Surface that still has an `Omarchy` entry, the command can no longer offer its “Disable direct boot” action:

| Same state: Microsoft BIOS vendor, existing entry, prerequisites pass | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Base | Offers removal; confirmation reaches `--delete-bootnum` |
| PR | Exits with the Surface error before lookup or confirmation |

This follows from source inspection and was corroborated with synthetic DMI inputs and stubbed EFI commands.

**Impact:** Users who enabled direct boot previously lose the command's built-in way to undo it and must use another removal method. This applies only while the entry still exists; it does not establish a boot failure.

**Suggested change:** Apply the new Microsoft refusal only to entry creation, preserving removal of existing entries. The same ordering already affects AMI/Apple, but changing those existing policies can remain separate.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned base/head source review and isolated synthetic routing checks. No real Surface boot, firmware, NVRAM, Secure Boot or entry deletion was tested; the reported firmware behavior remains unverified.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, then verification of the claim against source and targeted synthetic evidence. A fresh Astra Medium check covered presentation and privacy, not technical correctness.
